newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta hunger strikers vow to fight on in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Delta hunger strikers vow to fight on in Frankfurt.

text.p: Delta Air Lines staff on hunger strike at Frankfurt airport vowed on Saturday to continue their protest over job cuts, just hours after one of them received urgent medical treatment.

Ibrahim Keklik was back at his post in front of the airline's check-in desk in the afternoon. He was taken earlier to the airport clinic for a blood transfusion after he became weak and disoriented and lost feeling in his hands.
"He is quite well now and he wants to go on. He only agreed to be treated on condition he could come back," fellow hunger striker Ayhan Dagtekin told Reuters.
"The doctors have been advising us about our health and gave us multi-vitamin pills to keep us going," he added.
The conflict between the airline and its employees centres on Delta's plans to cut staff from 850 to 250 in Frankfurt and drop eight of its 14 daily flights.

Delta's works council wants job guarantees for the 250 remaining staff and wants Delta to invest 180 million marks, or its expected financial improvement from the restructuring measures, in a social plan valid until 2003.
Delta could not be contacted for comment. The airline has said in the past that union demands were unrealistic but that it was ready to talk.
Talks were in progress between Delta and the works council on Saturday afternoon aimed at settling the dispute, but the strikers said they were pessimistic about the chance of an agreement.
Earlier, works council chairman Walter Czogolla said the strike would continue "until we get an offer worth negotiating."
The four men and a woman involved in the protest have been mainly surviving on orange juice, coffee and vitamin pills.
"I am offering myself up for all the workers," said Dagtekin, looking alert and robust. "The health issue is not a factor for me. I will go on to the death."
